item.text: The forwarder currently caches whole `clusterSession` objects, and the Kubernetes service does not start the session uploader. I’ll cache only the short lived certificates, keep session state per request, and initialize the uploader during service startup.

	if f.Clock != nil {
		return f.Clock.Now()
	}
	return time.Now()
}

func (f *Forwarder) getCertificate(ctx authContext) (*tls.Config, error) {
	key := ctx.key()
	f.Lock()
	if cached, ok := f.certificates.Get(key); ok {
		cert := cached.(*tls.Config)
		if len(cert.Certificates) > 0 && cert.Certificates[0].Leaf != nil && cert.Certificates[0].Leaf.NotAfter.After(f.clockNow().Add(time.Minute)) {
			f.Unlock()
			return cert, nil
		}
		f.certificates.Remove(key)
	}
	f.Unlock()

	wait, cancel := f.getOrCreateRequestContext(key)
	if cancel == nil {
		select {
		case <-wait.Done():
			return f.getCertificate(ctx)
		case <-f.ctx.Done():
			return nil, trace.BadParameter("forwarder is closing, aborting the request")
		}
	}
	defer cancel()
	cert, err := f.requestCertificate(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, trace.Wrap(err)
	}
	if len(cert.Certificates) > 0 && cert.Certificates[0].Leaf != nil && cert.Certificates[0].Leaf.NotAfter.After(f.clockNow().Add(time.Minute)) {
		f.Lock()
		err = f.certificates.Set(key, cert, ctx.sessionTTL)
		f.Unlock()
		if err != nil {
			return nil, trace.Wrap(err)
		}
	}
	return cert, nil
}

item.text:
Fixed the Kubernetes exec startup issue. The Kubernetes service now creates the session streaming directory and starts its uploader. The forwarder caches credentials instead of request scoped sessions, keeps audit recording alive after client disconnects, and emits final exec audit events when streaming fails.

Verified with `go test ./lib/kube/proxy ./lib/service` and `git diff --check`; both passed.
